title: Hillbilly and jazz musicians compared; Benny Strickler with Bob Wills
summary: Parker says the best hillbilly and best jazz players fit anywhere. Crawford adds that trumpeter Benny Strickler played on Bob Wills records.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Do you make any distinction between the Hillbilly musicians and the other musicians you've played with?

Well, not these good ones. These good ones I'm talking about can fit anywhere and do anything. And the rest of them couldn't do anything in the first place. But you often find that in jazz musicians. Somebody had no business being there. You know, you get lost, bud. But among the, yes, indeed. And the very best of the Hillbilly musicians and the best of the jazz musicians would have no trouble at all. Would sit right there and there and go right on with no question and nothing to give them any separation at all. Not the slightest. I see Paul nods his head at this. He couldn't curse and so on. He's always, I've liked it whenever you nodded your head at what I'm saying. This is so, Paul.
I'm nodded more frequently. I know. I've heard some of them. This is true. Yeah, I know.

The good Hillbilly musicians fit easily into any good ensemble anywhere. Swing, jazz, either one. Drag, and the, uh, that's right. And the same, the reverse also. And this is interesting too. In, uh, later, in your late period there of this Bob Wills, so often he would have swing musicians come into his group. And if they were good swim musicians, they fit well into it. That's what you're getting into those late days after I left the Do Boys. And I don't know much about this. But I do know I kept hearing about names. Some trumpet player who died. Benny Strickler. Benny Strickler is one of them. Yeah. And speak about this please, because this bears out my whole thing.

That's all I know. Tell them who he was. He was a trumpet player from Oklahoma, wasn't he originally? Or, I don't know. Maybe he was here. I thought he was here. No, I don't think so. Did he ever play in New Orleans? He may have. I don't know. I read something about him, and my memory is not as good as yours, and Dick Allen's. And all I know is he went out and he played with, I think he did some subbing with Lil Waters, and Turk, and all that gang. But he was maybe making a living. No, he was playing with Bob Wills.
Yes, lots of records with Bob Wills. He fit in ideally. Yeah. That's the theory at any rate I was talking about. A good musician can do anything, and that's it.
Well, the music's worse. I mean, a good classical musician maybe or maybe couldn't fit into some of these other forms, but you felt the forms were close enough then.
